ChatGPT said:

Good — DNS and HTTPS are now fixed, so this 404 is not a domain problem anymore. The next most likely cause is the GitHub Pages build itself not publishing that new asset folder, even though the repo contains it.

GitHub’s own docs say branch-based Pages uses Jekyll by default, while adding an empty .nojekyll file at the root bypasses that processing and publishes the static site directly. GitHub Docs+1

Do this now:

  1. In the repository root, click Add file → Create new file.

  2. Name it exactly:

    .nojekyll

  3. Leave the file completely empty.

  4. Commit it directly to main.

  5. Wait for the new pages build and deployment action to finish successfully.

  6. Then test:

    https://www.rastarootslife.com/assets/home/home-hero-tea-ritual.png

That is the cleanest next move because your site is plain static HTML/CSS/JS and does not need Jekyll. GitHub specifically documents .nojekyll for this use case. GitHub Docs

If the image still 404s after that redeploy, the next step is to inspect the generated Pages artifact itself, because at that point we’ll know the file is being omitted during publishing rather than blocked by DNS, SSL, or path resolution.

  <script>
    (() => {
      const carousel = document.querySelector("[data-shop-carousel]");
      if (!carousel) return;
      const slides = [...carousel.querySelectorAll(".shop-slide")];
      const dots = [...carousel.querySelectorAll(".shop-carousel-dots button")];
      let index = 0;
      let timer;

      const show = (next) => {
        index = (next + slides.length) % slides.length;
        slides.forEach((slide, i) => slide.classList.toggle("is-active", i === index));
        dots.forEach((dot, i) => dot.classList.toggle("is-active", i === index));
      };

      const start = () => {
        if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches) return;
        timer = window.setInterval(() => show(index + 1), 5500);
      };

      dots.forEach((dot, i) => dot.addEventListener("click", () => {
        window.clearInterval(timer);
        show(i);
        start();
      }));

      show(0);
      start();
    })();
  </script>
